blocks.text: Sensitive data is confidential information such as personally identifiable information (PII), social security numbers, credit card information, financial data, login credentials, etc., that must be protected with strong security controls to prevent data breaches.

Knowing what type of sensitive data exists in your cloud environment and the resources where it is located is crucial to keep track and monitor this data regularly and ensure the data is secure. Data classification is an effective method to classify sensitive data, as this enables you to evaluate the risks and take immediate action to protect sensitive data.
DSPM supports data classification by using robust DLP engines and dictionaries that are synced from Internet & SaaS (ZIA).

You can only view the DLP engines in the Zscaler Admin Console. You can modify a DLP engine in Internet & SaaS if you have the necessary permissions. When modifying a predefined or custom engine, you can also combine dictionaries with Boolean operators to create logical expressions.
Data classification includes the following benefits and enables you to:

blocks.item: Classify sensitive data based on the level of sensitivity and risk.
View the DLP engines and dictionaries that are used by DSPM for data classification.
Manage the sensitivity settings for DLP engines.
Enable or disable the DLP engine evaluation.

blocks.heading: About the Data Classification Settings Page

blocks.text: On the Data Classification Settings page (Data Security > DSPM > Data Classification Settings), you can do the following:

blocks.item: This option is visible to users with permissions to view or edit the DLP Dictionaries & Engines page (Data Security > DSPM > Data Classification Settings).
View the list of DLP engines that are synced from Internet & SaaS. For each DLP engine, you can view:
DLP Engine Name: The name of the DLP engine.
Description: The description of the DLP engine.
Engine Type: The type (Predefined or Custom) of DLP engine.
Last Modified: The date and time the DLP engine was last modified.
Enabled: Whether the DLP engine evaluation is enabled or not.
Sensitive: The data sensitivity setting (enabled or disabled) for the DLP engine.
By default, the sensitivity setting is enabled for all DLP engines.
Enable or disable the DLP engine evaluation.
Disable the sensitivity setting for a specific DLP engine.
Search for a specific DLP engine.
